title: 11 known-answer PDFs, 44 drawn molecules — all three stages
corpus: 11 one-page PDFs; 44 molecules drawn across them
corpus_detail: Each page is a 2x2 grid of PubChem PNG depictions embedded at roughly 115-120 ppi with vector text labels. All 44 drawn molecules were verified pixel-exact against PubChem's depiction of their CID, so the ground truth is the SMILES of that CID.
stages: All three: VisualHeist figure extraction, DECIMER segmentation, then CXMolScribe.
method: Identical scoring to the stage-3 run: RDKit canonical SMILES, whole string and largest fragment, with and without stereochemistry. Structures are attributed to a document by the longest manifest stem that prefixes their figure name.
settings: CPU. Pipeline defaults; DECIMER_BBOX_PAD unset, i.e. 0, which is upstream behaviour.
note: A twelfth document, test_reactions_coupling.pdf, was run but has no molecule-level ground truth — it is reaction schemes, including Markush structures with R groups, which no single SMILES describes. Its structures appear at the bottom, shown and not scored. Compare this run with the stage-3-only run above rather than reading either alone: the difference between them is what segmentation costs.
